subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: What lifecycle policy should completed hook-agent sessions support, and how should it interact with generic session maintenance, cron retention, persistent hook sessions, and transcript retention?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the public config API, default behavior, transcript deletion/archive semantics, and upgrade safety are product and data-retention decisions.

options.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
options.body: Introduce a default-safe `hooks.sessionCleanup` style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

options.title: Rely On Generic Maintenance
options.body: Document that hook sessions are governed only by `session.maintenance` age/count/disk controls and close hook-specific cleanup as out of scope.

options.title: Defer Until Persistent Sessions Settle
options.body: Wait for the persistent hook-session direction before designing cleanup so reuse and deletion semantics are not contradictory.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-safe `hooks.sessionCleanup` style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already supplied the clearest product-direction review for this issue and is the strongest history signal for hook/config policy.
